risks.title: Office Real Estate Trends
risks.score_rationale: 78% of net operating income comes from office properties. Remote work, flexible schedules, and AI could reduce demand for physical space. Tenants prioritize modern, well-designed buildings near transit, creating intense competition among landlords and pressuring older buildings.

risks.title: Geographic Concentration
risks.score_rationale: The majority of net operating income is derived from the New York metropolitan area, exposing the company to regional economic fluctuations, local shocks, and real estate trends specific to NYC

risks.title: Real Estate Competition
risks.score_rationale: Highly competitive real estate market with numerous investors and property owners. Competition to attract tenants is increasing, particularly toward higher-quality buildings, impacting revenues and rental negotiation power.

risks.title: Tenant Credit Risk
risks.score_rationale: Exposure to credit risks related to tenant bankruptcy or insolvency, leading to reduced rental income, operational disruptions, and potential portfolio depreciation

risks.title: Climate Change and Real Estate Resilience
risks.score_rationale: The effects of climate change (flooding, storms, extreme heat) may damage properties, increase insurance, maintenance, and protection costs, reducing profitability

risks.title: Urban Safety Risks
risks.score_rationale: Properties concentrated in urban areas (NYC, Chicago, San Francisco) are exposed to safety risks. Incidents can affect property attractiveness, value, and tenant retention.

risks.title: Environmental Regulation and ESG Compliance
risks.score_rationale: Strict environmental regulations regarding greenhouse gas emissions, energy efficiency, and growing ESG compliance requirements. Compliance and improvement costs may be significant for the existing real estate portfolio.

ai_positioning.summary: Vornado mentions artificial intelligence as a potential factor affecting office tenant space utilization. In the 2025 10-K report, the company acknowledges that increased use of AI could result in changes in tenant space needs, including reductions or reconfigurations. This reflects broader concerns in the office real estate sector regarding AI's impact on demand for physical space.
evidence: Increased use of artificial intelligence (AI) could result in changes in tenant space utilization, including the need to reduce or reconfigure space (Risk Factors section)
